record.paper_title: Variation Structures: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For ε-hermitian variation structures of a group G, form the Witt group WVε(G) by quotienting isomorphism classes under direct sum by hyperbolic structures. For G=Z^k, the known classification decomposes WVε(G) over unitary characters χ and has summand Z for χ≠1 and Z2 for χ=1. How can this Witt-group classification be extended to more general groups, ideally to local fundamental groups of complements of curve singularities p^{-1}(0)⊂(C^2,0)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\varepsilon \in \{+1,-1\}$ and let $G$ be a group. An $\varepsilon$-hermitian variation structure over $G$ is a quadruple $(U; b, h, V)$ where $U$ is a finite-dimensional complex vector space, $b: U \times U \to \mathbb{C}$ is a non-degenerate $\varepsilon$-hermitian form, $h: G \to \mathrm{Aut}(U,b)$ is a representation by $b$-isometries, and $V: U \to U$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-linear endomorphism satisfying the compatibility conditions making $(U;b,h,V)$ an $\varepsilon$-hermitian variation structure in the sense of Némethi. A variation structure is called hyperbolic if it is isomorphic to a standard hyperbolic model on $U \oplus U^*$. Direct sum $\oplus$ endows the set of isomorphism classes with the structure of a commutative monoid, and the quotient
$$WV_\varepsilon(G) := \{\text{iso. classes of }\varepsilon\text{-hermitian variation structures over }G\}/\{\text{hyperbolic structures}\}$$
is an abelian group, called the Witt group of $\varepsilon$-hermitian variation structures of $G$.

For $G = \mathbb{Z}^k$, $WV_\varepsilon(\mathbb{Z}^k)$ decomposes as a direct sum indexed by unitary characters $\chi \in \widehat{G}$, and
$$WV_\varepsilon(\mathbb{Z}^k)_\chi \cong \begin{cases} \mathbb{Z} & \text{if } \chi \neq 1, \\ \mathbb{Z}/2 & \text{if } \chi = 1, \end{cases}$$
with explicit generators $(\mathbb{C}; \pm i^{(1-\varepsilon)/2}, \chi, \pm(\chi-1)i^{(\varepsilon-1)/2})$ for $\chi \neq 1$ and $(\mathbb{C}; 0, 1, 0)$ for $\chi = 1$.

Problem: Extend this classification of $WV_\varepsilon(G)$ to more general groups $G$. In particular, obtain a classification theorem when $G$ is the local fundamental group $\pi_1(B \setminus p^{-1}(0))$ of the complement of a plane curve singularity germ $p^{-1}(0) \subset (\mathbb{C}^2, 0)$, where $B$ is a small ball around the origin.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a problem list on variation structures. Web search reveals continued research on hermitian variation structures (e.g., work relating real Seifert forms, Hodge numbers and Blanchfield pairings) but no general classification theorem of $WV_\varepsilon(G)$ for arbitrary $G$, nor for local fundamental groups of plane curve singularity complements. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Real Seifert forms, Hodge numbers and Blanchfield pairings
status_evidence.snippet: Connections between Picard-Lefschetz invariants of isolated hypersurface singularities and Blanchfield forms for links, with Hermitian Variation Structures playing a unifying role.
status_evidence.claim: Active research continues on hermitian variation structures, but no general Witt-group classification beyond Z^k is established.
